sentences.text: Linlongopterus translates to "forest dragon wing," a name honoring Elfriede Kellner, known as Jenny, after whom the species L. jennyae is named.
This large flying reptile possessed a bony eye socket positioned lower on the skull than seen in other pteranodontoids.
First named in 2015, the fossil was found in Jianchang County, Liaoning province, and required gluing two separate blocks together for preparation.
The genus was formally described by Taissa Rodrigues, Shunxing Jiang, Xin Cheng, Xiaolin Wang, and Alexander Kellner in a 2015 paper.
Its teeth were likely adapted for a piscivorous diet, similar to other pteranodontoid pterosaurs.
It is likely placed within Anhangueria, though the lack of jaw crests and uniform tooth size suggests it was not an anhanguerid.
The time range for Linlongopterus is estimated from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
A 2024 study found Linlongopterus to be a primitive member of Ornithocheiriformes, sharing tooth size variation with Haopterus, which contrasts with earlier placements in Istiodactyliformes.
